findings.title: Expiry boundary and unknown-uid paths of ConsumeMemoShareView are untested
findings.failure_scenario: Change `expires_ts >= ?` to `expires_ts > ?` in the consuming UPDATE at store/db/sqlite/memo_share.go:218 (or in the mysql/postgres drivers). All tests still pass. The only expiry test, TestMemoShareConsumeRejectsExpired, sets expiry 10s in the past (line 244), so it never reaches expires_ts == now. The plan's assumption 'a share is expired when now is greater than expires_ts' makes that boundary a real contract, and nothing pins it. No test consumes an unknown uid either.
findings.evidence: memo_share_test.go:244 `expires := time.Now().Unix() - 10`; sqlite/memo_share.go:218 `WHERE uid = ? AND (expires_ts IS NULL OR expires_ts >= ?) AND (view_limit IS NULL OR view_count < view_limit)`. Context pack PLAN assumptions: 'Expiry in the consuming UPDATE keeps today's rule: a share is expired when now is greater than `expires_ts`.' The consume tests at lines 206-296 are the only callers of ConsumeMemoShareView in the test file, and none uses expires == now or a missing uid.
findings.fix: Add a case with expires == now that expects a successful consume, and one with expires == now-1 that expects nil. Add a case for an unknown uid that expects nil and no error. Add a case for view_limit 0 that expects nil.
findings.verification_note: I read all of store/test/memo_share_test.go. The consume tests (lines 206-296) cover the limit, no limit, an expiry 10s past, the listing and the race. None passes `now` equal to expires_ts, so the `>=` to `>` mutation survives, as the finding says. The production code at sqlite/memo_share.go:218 is correct today and matches the plan's expiry rule. That makes this a test-coverage gap with no concrete harm yet, so it stays minor (no-harm-yet). The unknown-uid path returns nil because sql.ErrNoRows maps to nil at lines 222-223, and no test covers it. A view_limit of 0 is not part of this task's acceptance criteria and may be rejected by API validation outside this task, so that part of the suggested fix is optional. Line 240 is the expired-share test's declaration and the 10s offset is at line 244, so I kept line 240.

notes:
Migration 26.10/00__add_memo_share_view_limit.sql added for sqlite, mysql and postgres. Schema version is now 26.10.1. LATEST.sql in each driver gains view_limit (nullable) and view_count (NOT NULL DEFAULT 0). store.Store.ConsumeMemoShareView(ctx, uid, now) returns (*MemoShare, error). It returns nil, nil when the share is missing, expired (now > expires_ts), or used up. On success the returned share carries the incremented ViewCount and ViewLimit. CreateMemoShare writes view_limit when set, and Create/List/Get all return ViewLimit and ViewCount. Test updates: migrator_test.go now expects 26.10.1 for a fresh install. migrator_guardrail_test.go's "calver-newer" case moved from 26.9.1 to 26.10.2. migrator_stable_upgrade_test.go still expects 0.31.8 after the released v0.31.0 binary runs, so it was left unchanged. The sqlite tests were run; the MySQL and PostgreSQL code is written but not run. The slice gate only builds the memos area (area.build-only nit), so the prove run was not exercised under the slice tier.
